title: Node.js command-injection false positive — execFile with an argument array
anti_example_patterns: Sink is parameterized/safely encoded by framework guarantees
note: The shape that triggers a reflex 'command injection' report: user input reaching a process spawn. It is not exploitable — execFile bypasses the shell entirely, args are passed as argv, and the host is allowlisted by regex first. Suppression Rule 3. Residual risk is that a later edit swaps execFile for exec, which is what the note must say.
allowed_adjacent_note: argument injection via a leading dash (CWE-88) is a different and legitimate finding; so is unbounded concurrent process spawning. CWE-918 is justified: `pingHost` sends ICMP to a caller-supplied hostname, so an attacker can probe internal hosts and infer topology from the timing/output even though no shell is involved. The fixture tests command injection; internal-host probing is a genuinely different and real finding in the same snippet, and Run 3 flagged it before this list did.
